scope: Every work in Beta maṣāḥǝft's Works repository tagged Old or New Testament or Bible whose edition division carries at least 200 Ethiopic characters, and the works of the Ethiopian canon the project tags otherwise (Jubilees, 1–3 Meqabyan, the Ethiopic Ezra apocalypse and the Ethiopic Ezra, 4 Baruch = Paralipomena of Jeremiah), the Sinodos canons, and three works read beside the canon (the Ascension of Isaiah, the Preaching of Peter, Yosippon). 1 Enoch, also in the canon, is seated in its own seat (EA-CORPORA-02/20, ethiopic-enoch), whose text layer this seating supplies. The Kebra Nagast is seated beside it (EA-CORPORA-20/02). The completeness of each book is Beta maṣāḥǝft's: a work's line count is in its entry, and a book edited only in part there is seated in part. Not seated (edition division present, under 200 Ethiopic characters): Introduction to the New Testament Epistles and the Revelation of John (LIT3199Introd, 0); ... as he says the names of Lofḥam (= Lot) ... (LIT7444PPLofham, 189); Amharic Psalter (LIT7743PsalterAmh, 148); Protective prayer: Psalm 90 (LIT7582PPPsalm, 131); Commentary on the Books of Kings (LIT6837CommentaryKings, 0); LIT6779Annun (LIT6779Annun, 0); Synopsis of classes (LIT1548Gessaw, 109); Four Gospels (LIT1560Gospel, 0); Ethiopic explanation of several Hebrew names (LIT5810ExplanationHebrewNames, 27); The Discourse of Dionysius on the Tribes of the Apostles (LIT5549TribesApostles, 179); The psalms of David resemble a garden... (LIT5884IntroHymnPs, 98); Protective prayer: Psalm 1:1–4 (LIT5823MagicPrayer, 183); Who is resting... (LIT5843ShortPoemMary, 118); Mark 1:23-27 (LIT7276MarkOne, 98); Introduction on the Reliability of the Gospels (LIT4875Reliability, 167); Praise of Mary (LIT2509Weddas, 73); Now you dismiss (LIT2272salota, 0). The Ethiopian Book of the Covenant (Maṣḥafa Kidān), the Didascalia (Dǝdǝsqǝlǝyā) and the Clement (Qalēmenṭos) of the broader canon carry no edition text there: QUEUED.

why_seated: The archive holds the Hebrew Bible (Westminster Leningrad Codex), the Septuagint (Swete), the Greek New Testament and the Dead Sea Scrolls; the canon that kept Enoch and Jubilees whole, and the only one in which they survive complete, was not on the shelf. Its Old Testament is the widest of any church's: Jubilees, Enoch and the three books of Meqabyan are scripture there. The archive's Revelation line reads the apocalypses as a tradition; this is the tradition in which they were kept.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-23: "detour for an ea-corpora searing. lets see. whats available of mayan texts? and then i dont think we have much or any deteurocanonical second temple lit - all those apocalypses. and what about the ethiopian canon? and euclid. all in original language or as close to it as possible. what else?" — "and the Egyptian book of the dead" — "and what about the fragments of the book of baalim?" — "yes yes yes to all - what a meal."
